details: US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data for May showed a 4.1% year-on-year increase for the headline index and 3.4% for core PCE, the highest since April 2023 and October 2023 respectively. This hotter-than-expected inflation has reduced market expectations for imminent Federal Reserve interest rate cuts, with some analysts suggesting the Fed may keep policy restrictive for longer or even consider future rate hikes. This macroeconomic shock triggered significant liquidations across crypto markets, contributing to Bitcoin's decline.
title: US Inflation Dampens Rate Cut Hopes, Bitcoin Falls

details: Over $1 billion in cryptocurrency positions were liquidated in the last 24 hours as Bitcoin's price fell sharply to approximately $59,000, reaching its lowest level since late 2024. This significant downturn impacted around 178,000 market participants. The decline is attributed to several factors including continued outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs, major Bitcoin sales by institutional entities like Strategy Inc., and escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly involving Iran.
title: Bitcoin Plunges Below $60K Amid Geopolitical Tensions & ETF Outflows

details: Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari, typically a dovish policymaker, stated he now expects one interest rate increase in 2026 and foresees rates remaining high for longer. This shift follows the Federal Reserve's recent June policy meeting where nine of 18 officials projected at least one rate hike this year. The change in outlook, coupled with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's move away from explicit forward guidance, increases market sensitivity to economic data and adds pressure on speculative assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Fed Official Signals Potential 2026 Rate Hike, Adding Market Pressure
